---
title: "Getting started"
description: "Install RiX in the RatMath workspace, run the REPL, execute scripts, and embed the evaluator."
---

RiX uses Bun. The package is an active alpha and is not yet presented as a
stable registry release: the public npm name `rix` belongs to an unrelated
project. Standalone development installs the compatible `@ratmath/core` 0.4
release.

## Requirements

- [Bun](https://bun.sh/) 1.2 or newer
- Git
- Quarto 1.6 or newer only if you want to build this documentation site

## Clone and test

```sh
git clone https://github.com/jostylr/ratmath.git
cd ratmath
bun install
bun --cwd rix test
```

The standalone repository supports `bun install` and `bun test`; the RatMath
umbrella workspace instead links its local Core checkout.

The RiX test suite exercises tokenizer, parser, lowering, evaluator, runtime, CLI, examples, exact values, types, methods, Shaped storage, mathematical tensors, generators, and diagnostics.

## Open the REPL

From the RatMath repository root:

```sh
bun run rix
```

```text
rix> 1/3 + 1/6
1/2
rix> Sq(x) -> x^2
<function Sq(x) ...>
rix> Sq(12)
144
rix> 23.456? < 23.4565
?
rix> ? ?: "yes" ?_ "no" ?? "not decided"
"not decided"
```

The question mark inside a number creates a certified approximation with an
exact rational enclosure. A standalone question mark is an undecided decision;
it is distinct from null (`_`) and can be handled by the `??` branch of the
three-state conditional.

Executable documentation examples use the same evaluator as the CLI. A
trailing `##@` assertion checks a value, and a standalone `##` asks the
documentation build to render the most recent result:

```{.rix exec=true id=getting-started-rational}
##SETUP##
half = x -> x / 2
##SETUP##
1 |> half ##@ == 1/2
##
```

Useful REPL commands include `.help`, `.vars`, `.fns`, `.ast[expr]`, `.tokens[expr]`, `.load[pkg]`, `.reset`, and `.exit`. End a line with `\` for multiline input.

## Persistent REPL setup

RiX keeps CLI configuration under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/rix`, falling back to
`~/.config/rix`. Set `RIX_CONFIG_DIR` to use another location. Create or update
the configuration with:

```sh
rix setup --plugins=full
rix setup --plugins=float,renderers
```

Plugin names and plugin groups are case-insensitive. `full` selects the
standard first-party plugin set; `renderers` selects Terminal ASCII, SVG,
Canvas-plan, TikZ, PNG, Markdown, HTML, Quarto, LaTeX, PDF, GIF, glTF, and CSV.
`.draw`, `.plot`, `.scene3d`, and `.nd` are producers and remain in their own
groups. RiX stores the selectors rather than expanding groups permanently, so
new standard plugins or group members can join later releases. Specialist
plugins outside `full` remain available by ID; for example, `--plugin=oracle`
loads the implemented exact Oracle plugin.

`rix setup` also creates `cli-preamble.rix` in the configuration directory. Its
leading YAML comment can request more plugins or operator files, and its RiX
body runs before each REPL starts:

```rix
/**
plugins: [float]
operator-files: [personal.operators.rix]
**/

digits := 50;
```

Use `--no-config` for a clean session, `--no-preamble` to retain configured
plugins without running the preamble, or `--preamble=FILE` for an explicit
project preamble. `--plugin`, `--plugins`, and `--operator-file` remain
one-session additions. Persistent setup affects the REPL, not script execution.

## Run a file

```sh
bun run rix ./rix/examples/eval/units-and-exact.rix
```

Or, from inside `rix/`:

```sh
bun bin/rix.js examples/eval/cayley-polar.rix
```

Native RiX test files use the `.test.rix` suffix:

```sh
bun bin/rix.js test
bun bin/rix.js test diagnostics
```

## Inspect the intermediate representation

```sh
bun run rix-to-ir --pretty ./rix/examples/eval/factorial.rix
```

The `rix-to-ir` command exposes the call-shaped IR used by the evaluator. Add `--lang` to prefix generated system calls with `@_`.

## Embed RiX in JavaScript

```js
import {
  Context,
  createDefaultRegistry,
  createDefaultSystemContext,
  parseAndEvaluate,
} from "rix";

const context = new Context();
const registry = createDefaultRegistry();
const systemContext = createDefaultSystemContext();

const result = parseAndEvaluate("x := 7; x^2 + 1", {
  context,
  registry,
  systemContext,
});
```

The public package also exports narrower entry points from `rix/parser`, `rix/eval`, and `rix/runtime`. See the [developer guide](developer-guide.qmd) for the pipeline and extension boundaries.

## Build this documentation

Install [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) and run:

```sh
cd rix
bun run build:docs
```

The build refreshes source-derived runtime reference tables, bundles the browser parser demo, validates the documentation inputs, and renders the site into `rix/docs/`. That output directory is suitable for GitHub Pages with **Deploy from a branch**, using the `main` branch and `/docs` folder.

For local authoring:

```sh
bun run preview:docs
```

Do not hand-edit `rix/docs/`; edit files in `rix/documentation/` and rebuild.
